impact_summary: GET /api/v1/items/ gains an optional case-insensitive `search` title filter (autoescaped icontains) combined with the existing owner scoping. The list/count logic for superuser and normal users was refactored into one shared filter path, and the Items page now has a search box (data-testid=item-search) that re-queries the API and shows a 'No items match your search' empty state. The refactor touches the owner-isolation logic, so regression risk is moderate.

cases_to_review.reason: List items own-only filtering was rewritten into a shared filters list; owner isolation must still hold with and without search.
The list endpoint handler was refactored; authentication requirement should be re-verified.
UI items list now uses a search-keyed query and a new empty-state branch; the logged-in user's-only display must still work.
Created item must still appear in the list; query key changed to ['items', search], which may affect cache invalidation after creation.
Edited item refresh depends on the items query key, which changed.
Delete-then-refresh and the empty-state text depend on the modified list component.

new_cases.title: Search items by title is case-insensitive and scoped to the caller's own items
steps: Create a new normal user A and a new normal user B, and log in as each to get tokens
As A, create items titled '<uniq>-Apple Pie' and '<uniq>-Banana Bread', where <uniq> is a random unique token
As B, create an item titled '<uniq>-apple Tart'
As A, call GET /api/v1/items/?search=<uniq>-APPLE with A's token
new_cases.expected: Response is 200; data contains exactly one item, titled '<uniq>-Apple Pie', owned by A. The match is case-insensitive, the non-matching Banana item and B's apple item are excluded, and count equals 1 (the unique token keeps this independent of any global counts).

new_cases.title: Search box filters the items list and shows the no-match empty state
steps: Sign up and log in as a new unique user (or create the user via API and log in via the UI)
Create two items via the API for that user, titled '<uniq>-Alpha' and '<uniq>-Beta'
Open the Items page and wait for both items to be visible
Fill the input with data-testid='item-search' with '<uniq>-alpha' (lowercase) and wait for the list to update
Verify the table shows '<uniq>-Alpha' and does not show '<uniq>-Beta'
new_cases.expected: After the first search only the '<uniq>-Alpha' row is visible and '<uniq>-Beta' is hidden. After the no-match search, the text 'No items match your search' and 'Try a different search term' are displayed.
